segs: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בְּמִדְבַּר, חֵלֶק ג קיז, ב)
In the holy Zohar (Bamidbar, Zohar III 117b):
"On the first of the second month
in the second year" — and it is all one;
and this is called the month of Ziv,
an allusion to this month and year
that gives light to the moon,
It appears that the intent is
as we said in the previous maamar:
when "This month shall be for you" was said,
for it was still before the tenth plague,
when they had not yet been made whole
and only to Moshe and Aharon was it said,
"This month shall be for you the head of months."
And this is, as we have said many times,
that it is called Rosh Chodesh
because it is the head of the month,
is all the kedushah of the month;
and Nissan is "the head of months,"
for it includes the kedushah of all the months.
And then, in the first year,
Rosh Chodesh did not yet shine forth
in all the months, as was said;
for then Nissan, which corresponds to Avraham,
who was the beginning of the light,
as Chazal say in Bereishis Rabbah (2:3):
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham";
the radiant ones of the world
who give light to the world;
and then it gives light to the moon.
And this is what it says,
for the purpose of the world
is that Malchus Shamayim be recognized
who accept upon themselves the yoke of His kingship, Yisbarach;
and this is what is called "world."
And this is "The world is built with chesed" (Tehillim 89:3),
for it was created through Avraham,
which is the radiance of the blessings of the world, etc.;
and therefore it is called the month of Ziv,
for the radiance of everything comes forth from it;
and it is all one matter, etc."
It appears from the holy Zohar
that what is written in Sefer Yetzirah,
means the small vav, the vav of the full spelling,
which is the middah of Yosef.
and he is "the radiance of the blessings,"
for so Yaakov Avinu said to him,
and in his blessing are said
ו׳ לְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל בְּרָכָה [שָׁם מט, כה-כו],
and he said (ibid.), "They shall be upon the head of Yosef."
And this is what is said (Tehillim 133:3),
"כִּי שָׁם צִיוָּה ה׳ אֶת הַבְּרָכָה וְגוֹ'".
"For there Hashem commanded the blessing, etc."
And Yosef is called "of beautiful form,"
for he had a pure body,
וְהֵבִיא אַחַר כָּךְ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם קיח, א)
the pasuk, "Like the dew of Chermon
שֶׁיּוֹרֵד עַל הַרְרֵי צִיּוֹן וְגוֹ'" (תְּהִלִּים קלג, ג),
that comes down upon the mountains of Tziyon, etc." (Tehillim 133:3);
that is, from the dew of Atika,
for the drawing-down from Kesser Elyon
and that is the dew of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is from the primordial light
that was hidden away for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh
that to merit the primordial light
one must have the middah of tzaddik;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קסו, ב)
as the holy Zohar says (Zohar II 166b):
"הַאי אוֹר זָרַע לֵיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי,
"This light, the Holy One, blessed be He, sowed it, etc.,
and He set it out in rows
who is the gardener of the garden, etc."
"And this is the light of the world,
'From Tziyon, the perfection of beauty,' etc."
That is the middah of Yosef,
and he is the perfection of the world's beauty.
That is, there it says beforehand,
which is the light of the sun,
as it says (Koheles 1:5), "And the sun rises";
and the nations of the world count by the sun.
And it is written, "He shone forth from Mount Paran,"
for the children of Yishmael count by the moon
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק ג רפא, ב),
and this is what is called "hofia":
the radiance of the sun, its light,
that "hofia" is the radiance of the sun.
'May there be peace within your ramparts,' etc."
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק א קצז, ב,
וְנִתְבָּאֵר בִּפְרִי צַדִּיק קְדוֹשִׁים מַאֲמָר יא);
and explained in Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim, maamar 11);
and Yosef is also the vav
the vav that includes all the Avos;
and the hei is the middah of Malchus,
the moon that receives from the sun
And this is what is written in the gloss
on what the holy Zohar says
which came solely from the chesed of Hashem Yisbarach;
and Yetzias Mitzrayim was in the merit of Avraham,
and it was to him that the exile and the redemption were told.
"'And the tiferes' — this is Mattan Torah."
But what he wrote, that Iyar is Gevurah —
it alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
And to merit the light of Torah she'b'al peh
"a mighty one who conquers his yetzer,"
which is the middah of Yosef,
שֶׁאָמַר "אֶת הָאֱלֹקִים אֲנִי יָרֵא" [בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, יח],
and this is from the middah of Gevurah, "the Fear of Yitzchak";
that is, to rectify for the future:
to be a mighty one who conquers his yetzer.
And so it is brought in Pri Etz Chaim
correspond to the four letters of the Name Havayah,
and Iyar corresponds to the upper hei, Binah,
"and his heart will understand, and he will return";
that is, to rectify the past:
"to purify us from our kelipos, etc.,"
and to rectify the root of the corruption of the nachash,
which was to instill the feeling of one's own pleasure.
And this is the preparation for Mattan Torah,
וְאִיתָא בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי (שְׁקָלִים פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ג)
and it is brought in the Yerushalmi (Shekalim 3:3),
וְכֵן בְּמִדְרָשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ט),
and likewise in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:9),
from what is written (Vayikra 16:19), "And he shall purify it and sanctify it";
and holiness means words of Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קכא, א)
as the holy Zohar says (Zohar II 121a):
from the place called Kodesh, etc."
Gavriel as the angel of this month,
who is from the middah of Gevurah;
a mighty one who conquers his yetzer from here on.
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב יא, ב)
And it is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 11b):
"And whoever comes from the left side
as is written in the gloss
what is written in Rashi's commentary
(רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יא, א, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ)
that the Nissan of the solar season
extends into the Iyar of the lunar calendar."
But this is difficult: according to all opinions
Yitzchak was born on Pesach (Rosh Hashanah ibid.),
and Pesach is in the lunar Nissan!
are called the radiant ones of the world:
for Avraham was the beginning of the light,
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham";
and he began in words of Torah on his own,
and he had no rebbi, etc.";
and Yaakov Avinu's middah is truth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יא] "כִּי בָא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ",
as it says (Bereishis 28:11), "for the sun had set,"
and as stated in Bereishis Rabbah (68:10).
the moon that receives from the sun;
and his middah is Gevurah — Torah she'b'al peh,
"And when it is taken from Gevurah
it is called Torah she'b'al peh";
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קמב, א):
And so it is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 142a):
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב יד, ב):
And so it is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 14b):
"He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah,
Yitzchak in the secret of Tevunah, etc."
in people who go into exile?
Rather, these are the mighty ones of Torah,
for so it says of it (Bamidbar 21:14):
in the Book of the Wars of Hashem,' etc."
That is, in Torah she'b'al peh.
what the Gemara says (Rosh Hashanah ibid.),

and answers, "for it has radiance for the trees";
and why does it not answer,
and not the radiance of the world,

Now, the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah ibid.) says
who holds that the Avos were born in Tishrei,
it is called "the month of the Eisanim,"
because the mighty ones of the world were born in it.
since the radiant ones of the world were born in it?
But one can say regarding their dispute
regarding their dispute about the creation of the world,
that both are the words of the living Elokim:
that in Tishrei it arose in thought to be created,
but it was not created until Nissan;
and this is "the conception of the world."
one can say that the conception was in Tishrei:
that is, as it was in the Divine thought,
that there would be no corruption at all;
and then the Avos are called the mighty ones of the world,
as it says (Bamidbar 24:21), "Firm is your dwelling place" —
that they cannot be moved at all,
that there should be no claim against them whatsoever.
that the world would not endure
and needed the partnership of the middah of mercy,
אָז אַף אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
then even Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
who wished to bring the whole world
under the wings of the Shechinah,
succeeded only for the days of his life
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק כט).
(as stated in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 29).
And likewise Yaakov: though his offspring were complete,
nevertheless only in the future will it become clear that
וּלְעֵת עַתָּה יֵשׁ עֲלֵיהֶם קִטְרוּגִים עוֹד.
but for now there are still accusations against them.
So they are called only the radiant ones of the world,
who give light to Knesses Yisrael,
who are first in the Divine thought —
"for the sake of Yisrael, who are called 'reishis'"
there are still accusations against Yisrael,
and so they are called "radiant ones" and not "mighty ones."
his middah was Gevurah and restraint,
and we do not find regarding him
that he sought to make converts,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פד, ד).
as stated in Midrash Rabbah (Bereishis Rabbah 84:4).
under the wings of the Shechinah,

as the holy Zohar says (Zohar II 14b):
and from Binah judgments are aroused,

the month of Iyar is called "Ziv"

he lists the first three weeks of the Sefirah
as corresponding to Chochmah, Binah and Daas;
and the beginning of the month of Iyar,
which is the third week of the Sefirah, is Daas.
And the intent is also as was said:
that Daas is the fiftieth gate
of the fifty gates of Binah,
which was revealed to baalei teshuvah;
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֵרוּשׁ רַשִׁ"י, כִּי תִשָּׂא לא, ג),
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ן, בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב, א).

is called Kodesh and is called Chochmah" —
we call it Torah she'b'al peh,
and they call it ruach hakodesh" —
meaning, a spirit from that Kodesh above.

עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִילָּה יד, ב),
is along the lines of what the Gemara says (Megillah 14b),
וְכֵן בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קסט, ב):
and likewise the holy Zohar (Zohar III 169b):
And this is what the Midrash says
(בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה חוּקַּת יט, ו, וְתַנְחוּמָא חֻקַּת ח):

were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues";
שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵרָע,
for Moshe Rabbeinu knew nothing at all of evil,

for he was like Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,

for when he was born the house was filled with light
Which is not so with Rabbi Akiva,

that this month is auspicious for teshuvah.
and the main thing is the healing of the soul.

from Pesach until Shavuos are beneficial";
